text:
Richard Stallman, born on March 16, 1953, in New York City, developed an early interest in computers, beginning with reading IBM 7094 manuals in his pre-teen years. He excelled at Harvard University before enrolling at MIT, where he became a regular in the hacker community, often known by his initials, RMS. During his tenure at MIT's AI Laboratory, he published early work on intelligent backtracking and worked on software projects such as TECO and Emacs.
Stallman became a vocal critic of the growing trend toward proprietary software and restrictive licenses, which he viewed as blocking user freedom. This concern led to the foundation of the GNU project in September 1983. His 1985 GNU Manifesto outlined his goal of creating a free operating system compatible with Unix. Stallman popularized the concept of copyleft, implemented in the GNU General Public License (GPL). He has consistently advocated for software freedom as a moral value, distinct from the development model of open-source software.
